description: Verify that DUT TCP uses 2*MSL upper bound on data-segment RTO (RFC 1122 §4.2.3.1 p96 SHOULD)
approach:
[Objective]
RTO must cap at some upper bound — without one the back-off would grow forever. RFC 1122 §4.2.3.1 SHOULDs 2*MSL. Linux uses tcp_rto_max=120 s which equals 2*60 s MSL.

[Scenario — chronological]
1. Handshake → DUT data → tester drops all.
2. DUT retransmits with doubling RTO.
3. After many doublings: TCP_INFO query → RTO should plateau at ≤ 2*MSL.

[Pass condition]
RTO plateau at 2*MSL (or smaller).

[Fail condition]
• Fail_handshake_did_not_complete
• Fail_query_failed — TCP_INFO query failed
• Fail_no_retx — no retransmits observed in kernel
• Fail_rto_above_2msl_cap — RTO exceeds 2*MSL
• Fail_rto_below_2msl_cap — observation budget exhausted before plateau

verdicts.Pass: DUT data RTO plateaued at 2*MSL — normal
verdicts.Fail_rto_above_2msl_cap: RTO plateau above 2*MSL (Linux RTO max 120 s exceeds spec)
verdicts.Fail_rto_below_2msl_cap: RTO below 2*MSL did not plateau within observation budget
